ground_truth_methodology: Established by directly reading the cloned source at the pinned commit (Read/Grep on benchmarks/real_world_python/repos/django), verified line-for-line against the actual clone. Veyra was NOT used to produce any of this file.

queries.query: Where is Django's QuerySet class defined?
Where is Django's base Model class defined?
queries.expected_answer_summary: django.db.models.base.Model, defined at db/models/base.py:508, using the ModelBase metaclass.

queries.query: Where is the CSRF protection middleware implemented?
queries.notes: deliberate contrast with the Flask/FastAPI negative CSRF queries -- Django, unlike those two, DOES implement CSRF protection in-repo.

queries.query: What does django.contrib.auth.authenticate() actually call to check a user's credentials?
queries.ground_truth_location: django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:124 (def authenticate) iterates the configured AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS and calls each backend's own authenticate() method, e.g. ModelBackend.authenticate at django/contrib/auth/backends.py:65.
queries.expected_answer_summary: authenticate() (contrib/auth/__init__.py:124) loops over the configured authentication backends and calls each one's authenticate() method (e.g. ModelBackend.authenticate, backends.py:65) until one succeeds.

queries.query: What is Django's default Manager class actually built from?
queries.ground_truth_location: django/db/models/manager.py:176 -- class Manager(BaseManager.from_queryset(QuerySet)): Manager is dynamically generated from QuerySet via BaseManager.from_queryset().
queries.expected_answer_summary: Manager (manager.py:176) is not written directly against QuerySet by inheritance in the usual sense -- it's dynamically constructed by BaseManager.from_queryset(QuerySet), which copies QuerySet's public methods onto a generated Manager subclass.
queries.notes: tests whether retrieval surfaces the less-obvious from_queryset() dynamic-construction detail rather than a naive 'Manager inherits from QuerySet' answer, which would be wrong.

queries.query: How does an incoming WSGI request get dispatched to the correct Django view function, end to end?
queries.ground_truth_location: WSGIHandler (core/handlers/wsgi.py:113) is called by the WSGI server; it builds a request and calls BaseHandler.get_response (core/handlers/base.py:138), which calls the middleware chain, ultimately reaching _get_response (base.py:176), which resolves the URL (django.urls.resolvers.URLResolver.resolve, resolvers.py:670, via URLPattern.resolve at 471) and calls the matched view.
queries.expected_answer_summary: WSGIHandler (core/handlers/wsgi.py:113) receives the raw WSGI call and builds a WSGIRequest; get_response() (core/handlers/base.py:138) runs it through the middleware chain; _get_response() (base.py:176) resolves the request's path via the URL resolver (URLResolver.resolve, urls/resolvers.py:670) and calls the resulting view callback.

queries.query: How does Django apply configured middleware to every request?
queries.ground_truth_location: django/core/handlers/base.py:27 (load_middleware) wraps get_response in each configured middleware (outer to inner) and stores the result as self._middleware_chain (base.py:104); get_response (base.py:138) calls self._middleware_chain(request) (line 142).
queries.expected_answer_summary: load_middleware() (base.py:27) builds a nested chain of middleware callables around the core view-dispatch function, storing it as self._middleware_chain; get_response() (base.py:138) invokes that chain (line 142) on every request, so each configured middleware wraps the next one in order.

queries.query: What happens when CsrfViewMiddleware detects a POST request without a valid CSRF token?
queries.ground_truth_location: django/middleware/csrf.py:165 -- CsrfViewMiddleware's process_view rejects the request with a 403 Forbidden response rather than allowing it to reach the view.
queries.expected_answer_summary: CsrfViewMiddleware (middleware/csrf.py:165) rejects the request with a 403 Forbidden response instead of letting it reach the view function.

queries.query: What does authenticate() return if the given credentials don't match any configured authentication backend?
queries.ground_truth_location: django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:124 -- authenticate() returns None if no backend successfully authenticates the given credentials.
queries.expected_answer_summary: authenticate() (contrib/auth/__init__.py:124) returns None when no configured backend can authenticate the credentials.

queries.query: If a Django app's migrations aren't being applied in the order I expect, where should I look?
queries.ground_truth_location: django/db/migrations/executor.py:10 -- class MigrationExecutor, which resolves the migration dependency graph and determines execution order.
queries.expected_answer_summary: MigrationExecutor (db/migrations/executor.py:10) is responsible for resolving the dependency graph between migrations and determining the order they run in -- that's where ordering issues trace back to.

queries.query: Where would I investigate if a custom Manager isn't exposing a custom QuerySet method I defined?
queries.ground_truth_location: django/db/models/manager.py:176 -- Manager is built via BaseManager.from_queryset(QuerySet); a custom manager must be built the same way (Manager.from_queryset(MyQuerySet)) for its methods to be exposed on the manager.
queries.expected_answer_summary: Manager's methods come from BaseManager.from_queryset() (manager.py:176 shows the default Manager built this way from QuerySet) -- a custom QuerySet's methods only reach a Manager if the custom manager was itself built via Manager.from_queryset(MyQuerySet); that's the first place to check.

queries.query: How does registering a model in the admin (admin.site.register) connect it to Django's admin URLs?
queries.ground_truth_location: ModelAdmin (contrib/admin/options.py:686) defines the change-list/add/change views for a registered model; AdminSite.get_urls (contrib/admin/sites.py:258) builds the URL patterns for every registered ModelAdmin, which are then resolved through the same URLResolver machinery as any other Django URL.
queries.expected_answer_summary: admin.site.register() associates a model with a ModelAdmin instance (options.py:686); AdminSite.get_urls() (sites.py:258) iterates all registered models and builds URL patterns pointing at each ModelAdmin's views, which get included into the project's normal URL resolution.
queries.notes: cross-file: connects contrib/admin/options.py (per-model admin config) to contrib/admin/sites.py (URL wiring).

queries.query: Where does Django implement its own production-grade HTTP/2 server?
queries.expected_answer_summary: Django has no production HTTP/2 server implementation in this repository. It ships only a development server (runserver) and expects production deployments to use a separate WSGI/ASGI server (e.g. gunicorn, uvicorn) in front of it.

queries.query: Where does Django implement a built-in GraphQL API layer?
queries.expected_answer_summary: Django has no built-in GraphQL support in this repository. GraphQL support is provided by third-party packages (e.g. graphene-django), not Django core.
